rules: To appear in the policy table, a party must have a sitting MP or average 2% or more in recent nationwide polls, and must publish policies on its own website. Up to three policies per party per issue, taken in the order each party lists them and placed under the issue they best fit. Titles and summaries use the party's own wording. Parties shown in alphabetical order. Every party on the ballot is listed separately with a link to its website.

ACT.title: Abolish Labour's Rental Tax
ACT.summary: ACT will reverse another of Labour's renters' taxes by ending loss ring-fencing.

ACT.title: No Tax on KiwiSaver Earnings
ACT.summary: ACT will reward saving by letting you keep those earnings.

ACT.title: Open the Door to Supermarket Competition
ACT.summary: ACT will make it easier for new supermarkets to open and grow, so shoppers have more places to take their business.

Green.title: A tax system for all of us
Green.summary: The Green Party's tax plan will address inequality, tackle corporate greed, and tax income fairly. Includes a $10,000 tax-free threshold, a 2.5% tax on net assets over $10 million (family homes exempt), and a higher rate on income over $160,000.

Green.title: Affordable food for all of us
Green.summary: Our policy will reform the food system so that everyone has easy and affordable access to good, nutritious kai.

Green.title: New bill to ban supermarket price gouging
Green.summary: A law to make it illegal to charge unreasonable prices for groceries.

Labour.title: $20 Fare Cap
Labour.summary: $20 a week is the most you'll pay to get around by bus or train under Labour. In place by 1 July 2027.

Labour.title: Capital Gains Tax
Labour.summary: A simple, targeted 28% tax on profit from selling investment property after 1 July 2027.

Labour.title: Banning Price Gouging
Labour.summary: Making it illegal for big companies to overcharge for essentials.

National.title: No new taxes under National
National.summary: No new taxes so you keep more of what you earn.

National.title: Keeping rates affordable
National.summary: So families can keep more money in their pockets, with rates increases that are more affordable and predictable.

National.title: More grocery competition
National.summary: National will pursue a separation of New World and PAK'nSAVE so they compete harder against each other for shoppers.

NZ First.title: Break up the Supermarket Duopoly
NZ First.summary: New Zealand First will introduce legislation to reform the system and break up Foodstuffs.

NZ First.title: Lowering Tax Rate for SMEs to 20%
NZ First.summary: Lowering the company tax rate for SMEs to 20%, from 28%, for firms with turnover under $30 million.

NZ First.title: Establishing a KiwiSaver Generation
NZ First.summary: KiwiSaver enrolment compulsory at birth, with an automatic immediate Crown contribution of $1000.

Opportunity.title: Tax Reset
Opportunity.summary: It's time for a tax reset that increases incomes, makes homes affordable and safeguards retirement. Includes a Citizen's Income of up to $370 a week for almost all adults, funded by a 1.75% Land Value Tax, phased in over a decade.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Tax
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Make sure the wealthiest pay their fair share. Use that revenue to fund housing, health, education and whānau support.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Cost of living
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Lift incomes so people can live with dignity. Strengthen welfare so whānau aren't punished for being poor.

ACT.title: A Starship for Cancer
ACT.summary: ACT will support a world-class National Cancer Centre with campuses in Auckland and Christchurch.

ACT.title: Let Pharmacies Do More
ACT.summary: Widen what pharmacists can do and set clear rules for when a patient needs to see a doctor.

ACT.title: Strengthening End of Life Choice
ACT.summary: Implement all 25 recommendations from the Ministry of Health's statutory review of the End of Life Choice Act.

Green.title: Health (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Ensure public health care services are accessible for all with a focus on prevention and early screening.

Green.title: Health (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Fund mobile health care and mental health care clinics, diagnostics services and dental vans for rural communities.

Green.title: Health (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Work towards a publicly delivered, fully free provision of dental and primary care services.

Labour.title: Free Doctor's Visits
Labour.summary: Three free doctor's visits a year for everyone. Delivered with Labour's new Medicard.

Labour.title: Free Prescriptions
Labour.summary: Labour will remove the $5 fee on prescriptions to make them free for everyone. From 1 July 2027.

Labour.title: Free Maternity Scans
Labour.summary: Labour will make maternity scans free, everywhere in New Zealand with the Medicard. From July 2028.

National.title: More medicines and earlier care
National.summary: Delivering more medicines and earlier screening with no new taxes: a further $604 million for Pharmac's medicines budget, free bowel screening from age 50 by 2029, and free cervical screening for women aged 25 to 69 from March 2027.

NZ First.title: The Plan to “Make NZ Healthy”
NZ First.summary: New Zealand First will shift the focus of healthcare from treating illness to preventing it, including cutting paperwork for family doctors and placing health coaches in primary care.

Opportunity.title: Healthy People
Opportunity.summary: A protected 10-year plan that properly funds health workers and focuses on preventing illness, raising health funding from 7.4% to 9% of GDP over the decade.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Health
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Re-build and strengthen Māori-led health authority and solutions. Shift the system toward prevention and whānau wellbeing, not just crisis response.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Disabilities
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Support Māori-led disability services and decision-making. Make support easier to access and less degrading.

Green.title: Housing (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Build tens of thousands of new public homes, significantly increase accessible public housing stock, and fund more papakāinga on whenua Māori.

Green.title: Housing (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Make rents more affordable by limiting annual rent increases to no more than 2%.

Green.title: Housing (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Strengthen the Healthy Homes Standards and enforce them with an independently certified Rental Warrant of Fitness.

Labour.title: Start Work Now
Labour.summary: Labour will build the homes, improve the schools and repair the hospitals our communities need, including $2.9 billion of capital for Kāinga Ora to build more state houses.

National.title: Giving more Kiwis access to 5% first home deposits
National.summary: Make it easier to get a house deposit through the First Home Loan scheme, by raising the income cap to $300,000 for all applicants.

NZ First.title: Changes to Fast-Track Residential Approvals
NZ First.summary: Changes to the fast-track regime to ensure housing developments do not create more problems than they solve, requiring essential infrastructure to be approved before housing.

Opportunity.title: Affordable Housing
Opportunity.summary: Our plan to permanently narrow the gap between wages and house prices, while building the healthy homes our communities need, including replacing over 1,000 planning zones with 10 nationally consistent ones.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Housing
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Build and support more public and affordable homes. Make it easier to build homes on Māori/ancestral land. Stop speculation and land-banking.

ACT.text: No housing-specific policy is listed on ACT's policy pages (checked 15 Oct). ACT groups housing with infrastructure.

ACT.title: Keeping Children Safe
ACT.summary: One national card checked continuously for anyone, paid or unpaid, who works with children.

ACT.title: Real Choice for Students
ACT.summary: ACT will amend the regulations so universities must offer student services as a menu.

ACT.title: Affordable School Uniforms
ACT.summary: Limit state schools to a maximum of three compulsory branded uniform items.

Green.title: Education (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Make early childhood education free and provide it as a public good like schooling.

Green.title: Education (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Reset the Government's rushed and ideological curriculum and assessment reforms.

Green.title: Education (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Expand the criteria for access to learning support.

Labour.title: Cutting Student Debt
Labour.summary: A 10% cut to eligible student loan balances, with small balances under $2,000 written off completely.

Labour.title: Cutting Back-to-School Costs
Labour.summary: Cheaper uniforms, healthy school lunches back from Term 1 2028, rural school buses restored, and lower transport costs.

National.title: Teaching the basics brilliantly
National.summary: A world-leading education system that raises achievement, including replacing NCEA from 2028 with new senior secondary qualifications and a Learning Support Coordinator in every school with Year 1–8 students.

National.title: Back Pocket Boost for Graduates
National.summary: Reward young graduates who stay in New Zealand by cutting the student loan repayment rate from 12% to 10% from 1 April 2027, with tougher rules for overseas borrowers.

Opportunity.title: Future-fit Education
Opportunity.summary: A 10-year cross-party plan for education, focussed on stability for students, with an Independent Curriculum and Assessment Council setting curriculum rather than politicians.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Education & Training
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Build Māori-led education authority and solutions. Embed mātauranga Māori properly across learning. Remove barriers that block whānau from education and training.

NZ First.text: No education policy is listed on NZ First's policy page (checked 15 Oct).

ACT.title: Scrap Net Zero, Cut the Carbon Tax
ACT.summary: Scrap the arbitrary net zero 2050 target and repeal the Zero Carbon Act.

ACT.title: Abundant and Affordable Electricity
ACT.summary: Let you choose who buys your power, and lift unnecessary limits on your solar so households can export more power where the network has room.

ACT.title: Scrap the Climate Change Commission
ACT.summary: ACT will abolish the Commission and transfer its monitoring and reporting duties to the ministry that already measures emissions.

Green.title: Power for all of us
Green.summary: Lower bills. Cleaner energy. Public ownership. Includes $200 million for community energy projects and $80 million for renewable energy for Māori housing.

Green.title: Fast, frequent, affordable public transport for all of us
Green.summary: Fast, frequent and affordable public transport that saves people time and money, including $2 adult bus and train fares and up to 150 new regional bus services.

Green.title: Drink, Swim, Fish
Green.summary: The Green Party will fix the rules so all of us can drink, swim, and fish in the places we love, with strong, science-based national standards for freshwater.

Labour.title: SolarSaver
Labour.summary: Removes the barrier that locks most families out of solar power: low-interest finance with nothing to pay upfront, a subsidy of up to $3,000 for low- and middle-income households, and a $30 million community battery fund.

National.title: Home Energy Fund
National.summary: Help Kiwis become more energy independent and cut power bills, with long-term loans for solar, batteries, insulation and heat pumps repaid through rates, and rooftop solar without a consent.

National.title: Affordable power Kiwis can rely on
National.summary: A nine-point energy plan delivering more supply, more competition, and more choice for households and businesses, to help make power more affordable.

National.title: Hunting and Fishing
National.summary: National will strengthen hunter-led conservation and protect access to the outdoors.

NZ First.title: Breaking up the Gentailers
NZ First.summary: Breaking up the power companies so they can no longer control both the power and the price.

NZ First.title: Future Proofing our Fuel Security
NZ First.summary: An initial investment of $1 billion for a national survey of subsurface energy, geothermal and CO₂ storage sites.

NZ First.title: We Will Withdraw From The Paris Accord
NZ First.summary: New Zealand First is saying we need to get out of the Paris Accord altogether.

Opportunity.title: Abundant Energy
Opportunity.summary: A circuit breaker for an energy system that has been underfunded for decades, including a cross-party 30GW renewable capacity target for 2050.

Opportunity.title: Climate Action
Opportunity.summary: A $1 billion fund from ETS revenues to help industry move off coal and gas, and a $5 billion Climate Resilience Fund.

Opportunity.title: Healthy Land & Water
Opportunity.summary: Restore our land, clean up our rivers and treat nature as critical national infrastructure.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Energy Sovereignty
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Establish a $1 Billion Energy Sovereignty Fund and a National Independence Energy Plan.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Climate
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Protect whenua and moana from extractive industries (including banning seabed mining). Invest in climate resilience for communities most at risk.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Freshwater Policy
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Assert Māori rights and authority over freshwater. Stop decisions being made without Māori consent.

ACT.title: Deport Serious Offenders
ACT.summary: Ensure Resident Visa holders convicted of offences carrying sentences of 10 years or more can be deported, no matter how long they've been here.

ACT.title: Three Strikes for Burglary
ACT.summary: ACT will create a new Three Strikes regime for burglary.

ACT.title: Stopping Coercion by Animal Abuse
ACT.summary: Strengthen protections for pets used as instruments of coercion and control in family violence.

Green.title: Justice and Community Safety (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Resource evidence-based rehabilitation for anyone convicted of an offence.

Green.title: Justice and Community Safety (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: Expand Te Ao Mārama to all courts in Aotearoa.

Green.title: Justice and Community Safety (2026 manifesto)
Green.summary: End military-style academies and raise the age of criminal responsibility.

National.title: Modernise Sexual Consent Laws
National.summary: Modernise consent laws to require an explicit 'yes' rather than silence.

National.title: Tougher Sentences for Sexual Offending
National.summary: Real consequences for crime by removing good character assessments from sentencing for all sexual offences.

National.title: More Police on Auckland's buses and trains
National.summary: A dedicated Auckland Transport Police Team, so you feel safe catching public transport.

NZ First.title: Ban Public Sales of Fireworks
NZ First.summary: New Zealand First will campaign on banning the public sale and use of fireworks across New Zealand.

NZ First.title: All Gangs Should Be Terror Entities (petition)
NZ First.summary: New Zealand First calls for all gangs to be designated 'terrorist entities' under the Terrorism Suppression Act.

Opportunity.title: Smart On Crime
Opportunity.summary: An evidence-based plan to make New Zealand safer: voluntary interventions as soon as risk factors are identified, and growing specialist courts.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Justice
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Build Māori-led justice authority and community solutions. Reform laws that criminalise poverty and survival. Move away from mass imprisonment.

Labour.text: No crime and justice policy is listed on Labour's policy page (checked 15 Oct).

ACT.title: ACT's Fiscal Plan
ACT.summary: Balances the books without new taxes and starts paying down debt, with debt $12.4 billion lower by 2031 and the NZ Super age rising to 67 by 2035.

ACT.title: Local Tourism Dividend
ACT.summary: Return $1 to a community for every commercial guest night it hosts.

ACT.title: Backing Small Business
ACT.summary: So the people who build businesses and those who work for them can get ahead through their own effort.

Green.title: Good jobs for all of us
Green.summary: A plan to guarantee a job for every young person in Aotearoa, including 32,000 young people into local jobs through the Mayors Taskforce for Jobs.

Green.title: Economic development plan
Green.summary: A plan to rebuild Aotearoa New Zealand and create 284,000 jobs over four years.

Green.title: Plan for city centre vibrancy
Green.summary: A plan to get small businesses a fair deal.

Labour.title: New Zealand Future Fund
Labour.summary: An independently governed New Zealand Future Fund to invest in infrastructure and innovative Kiwi businesses.

Labour.title: Fiscal Plan
Labour.summary: Balance the books, return to surplus by 2028/29, and reduce net debt to below 20% of GDP.

Labour.title: AI in New Zealand's Interests
Labour.summary: Protect what matters, unlock our potential, and lead on our own terms with a new Office of AI.

National.title: National's plan to secure New Zealand's future
National.summary: A fiscal plan that prioritises bringing down debt and delivers surplus in 2028/29, with no new taxes.

National.title: Building the Future: National's Economic Plan
National.summary: So hardworking New Zealanders can keep more of what they earn, including replacing the RMA and debt below 40% of GDP over time.

National.title: National's plan to support Small Businesses
National.summary: A 47-point plan to grow the economy, back small businesses, spend sensibly and reduce debt without new taxes to create jobs.

NZ First.title: Returning 50% of mining royalties to the regions
NZ First.summary: 50% of any royalties gained from mining to be directly returned to the region from which it came.

NZ First.title: Backing a New Zealand Owned Bank
NZ First.summary: A buy-back of the Bank of New Zealand from National Australia Bank.

NZ First.title: The $100bn New Zealand Future Fund
NZ First.summary: A New Zealand Future Fund of up to $100 billion to invest solely in a multi-decade infrastructure build.

Opportunity.title: Breakthrough Economy
Opportunity.summary: Fund science, stand up for fairness and back small businesses, including a $600 million a year tax credit for technology adoption.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Economic development
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Build Māori-led institutions and funds that grow Māori enterprise. Support trade, innovation, and long-term Māori wealth building. Protect Māori data and knowledge.

ACT.title: Put 'Reside' Back in 'Resident'
ACT.summary: ACT will put 'reside' back in 'resident', including removing the existing Permanent Resident Visa category.

ACT.title: A Fair Contribution for Infrastructure
ACT.summary: ACT will add a $6-a-day infrastructure surcharge to temporary work visas.

Green.title: Immigration Policy
Green.summary: Increase our refugee quota and the resources required to provide adequate refugee services.

Green.title: Immigration Policy
Green.summary: Advocate for a Pacific Passport to allow for free movement between the islands and Aotearoa.

National.title: National's plan to welcome more Kiwis home
National.summary: Prioritising and expediting work and visitor visas for partners of New Zealand citizens, as part of five commitments in the first 100 days.

National.title: Making Trans-Tasman travel seamless
National.summary: Work with Australia to trial seamless travel for Australian and New Zealand citizens.

NZ First.title: Immigration Reform Policies
NZ First.summary: Sweeping changes to current immigration laws: only the children of citizens automatically entitled to citizenship at birth, and the qualifying period for citizenship doubled from five to ten years.

NZ First.title: Scrapping Accredited Working Visa Model
NZ First.summary: End the Accredited Employer Work Visa and replace it with a shortage-led Skilled Work Visa.

NZ First.title: Citizen's Only Voting
NZ First.summary: Change electoral law so only citizens can vote.

Labour.text: No immigration policy is listed on Labour's policy page (checked 15 Oct).

Opportunity.text: No immigration policy is listed on Opportunity's policy page (checked 15 Oct).

Te Pāti Māori.text: No immigration policy is listed on Te Pāti Māori's policy page (checked 15 Oct).

issues.name: Māori rights and the Treaty of Waitangi

ACT.title: Wind up the Waitangi Tribunal
ACT.summary: Complete every eligible historical claim already before the Tribunal, end its jurisdiction over contemporary Crown policy, and disestablish it once all eligible historical claims are completed.

ACT.title: One Law for All. One Future Together.
ACT.summary: One law for all means the same rights, the same duties, and the same protection under the law.

Green.title: Te Tiriti o Waitangi
Green.summary: Te Tiriti o Waitangi is the foundation for a just and thriving Aotearoa. The Green Party is committed to upholding Te Tiriti in everything we do.

Green.title: Te Waonui a Tāne
Green.summary: Recognise and resource marae as critical social and cultural infrastructure, with $2.44 billion in Crown funding for Te Rangatiratanga Trust.

Green.title: Ake, Ake, Ake: te reo Māori
Green.summary: An additional $50m per year towards te reo Māori initiatives.

Labour.title: Backing Māori into Skilled Work
Labour.summary: $21 million a year in Māori-led training that helps more whānau Māori gain skills and move into good, well-paid work.

NZ First.title: Disestablish Auckland's 'Independent Maori Statutory Board'
NZ First.summary: Disestablish the unelected Auckland Council Independent Māori Statutory Board.

NZ First.title: Referendum on Maori Seats
NZ First.summary: A referendum on the future of the Māori seats, so the public can decide if they are effective, relevant, and still needed.

NZ First.title: Ending the Waitangi Make-Work Industry
NZ First.summary: Legislation within the first 100 days to abolish the Waitangi Tribunal and replace it with a Treaty of Waitangi Completion Commission.

Opportunity.title: Honouring Te Tiriti
Opportunity.summary: Opportunity takes the responsibility of the Crown as a Treaty partner seriously: honour existing Treaty settlements, and restore the customary marine title settings that applied before the 2025 changes.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Te Tiriti Entrenchment
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Establish a Matike Mai Fund. Implement the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Mana Motuhake
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Commit to Te Tiriti-based constitutional change. Strengthen Māori political authority and governance structures.

Te Pāti Māori.title: Te Reo Māori
Te Pāti Māori.summary: Strengthen te reo Māori and normalise it everywhere. Invest in te reo Māori learning pathways and community-led language revitalisation.

National.text: No policy on Māori rights or the Treaty of Waitangi is listed on National's policy page (checked 15 Oct).
